text: Starting a new business is exciting, but it is rarely easy. An entrepreneur usually begins with a single idea and must find a way to turn it into a real product or service. Before they launch a startup, most founders need funding, which often comes from an investor who believes in the idea and expects a share of future profit in return. However, every venture involves risk: while some businesses grow quickly and succeed, others run out of money and end in failure. To attract funding, entrepreneurs often pitch their idea to investors, explaining how it is innovative and different from existing competitors in the market. A clear budget is essential because resources are usually limited in the early stages, and even a small loss can be dangerous for a new company. If a startup manages to build a strong brand and a loyal group of customers, it may be able to scale its operations and expand into new markets. Although many startups fail within the first few years, those that survive often say that learning from early mistakes was more valuable than any business course.
